status: PASS (A40): sweeps 100.00% equal to the XLA reference (92,691 tautomer calls, 0 differ), energies and site potentials bitwise equal (0.0), L2 vs DelPhi passes with the Pallas backend on 99 M0 states, SOR 10.2x faster, per-state total 3.5x faster than the XLA path, deterministic (bitwise across passes, tarball and fresh compile), SOR = 1 executable, compiles 33 = budget
design: sor.sor_solve: one Triton launch = one colour half-sweep for all W lanes on a (lane, 2048-point block) grid (launch boundary = red/black sync); flat zero-padded phi/rhs [W,NF] (OFF = ceil(n^2/BLK)*BLK); operator = uint8 code per point (bit0 ex, bit1 ey, bit2 ez in solute, bit3 ion) + 16-entry 1/diag table per operator (exact-integer diag partial sums -> bitwise the reference dinv); even colour first, fixed omega per lane, max-change < 0.01 checked every 10 sweeps, 500 cap, per-lane early exit (done lanes return at once), whole solve in a device while_loop (no host repacking); max over blocks is order-independent -> deterministic. One-program-per-lane rejected: needs a grid-wide barrier between colours inside one program (CTA barrier + global fence not exposed by Pallas) and gives only 256 CTAs of serial work.
xla_reference: kept (sor.run_pool); phase-2 coefficient table padded to E = 2B so sor_block compiles once per width (budget 3, was 6 in M1)
